questionText: A new curriculum has been introduced for Junior High Schools, but your school offers only a limited number of subjects. Write a letter to your headteacher suggesting two new subjects that should be taught in your school. Give two reasons for your choices.
modelAnswer:
CONTENT (10 marks): State two new subjects (4 marks) and explain how they will help students (6 marks).
ORGANIZATION (5 marks): Formal letter format requiring: Writer's address, Date, Recipient's designation and address, Salutation, Heading/Title, Body, Subscription, Signature, Full name.
EXPRESSION (10 marks): Formal language required. No slang or contractions.
MECHANICAL ACCURACY (5 marks): Deduct 1/2 mark per error up to 5 marks for grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors.

questionText: The government has announced the addition of new public holidays. Write an article to be published in a national newspaper on two effects of public holidays on teaching and learning.
modelAnswer:
CONTENT (10 marks): Discuss two positive or negative effects of public holidays on teaching and learning with illustrations.
ORGANIZATION (5 marks): Article format requiring: Title/Heading, Writer's name, Writer's address/designation.
EXPRESSION (10 marks): Formal and polite language.
MECHANICAL ACCURACY (5 marks): Deduct 1/2 mark per error up to 5 marks for grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors.

questionText: You once doubted your abilities, but an experience changed your mindset completely. Write your story, ending with the statement, 'I will never compare myself with anyone again.'
modelAnswer:
CONTENT (10 marks): A personal story that logically leads to and ends strictly with the given statement. Fables are not acceptable.
ORGANIZATION (5 marks): Story format with title, setting, and clear plot (beginning, climax, conclusion). Use of storytelling techniques like dialogue or flashback should be rewarded.
EXPRESSION (10 marks): Appropriate register, varied sentences, and effective use of figurative language.
MECHANICAL ACCURACY (5 marks): Deduct 1/2 mark per error up to 5 marks for grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors.
